_**User**_

Part B - Practical task
Create a fresh project yourself - create-next-app or Vite, your choice - and build one screen. There is no backend
and no API: generate the data locally.
An unfinished submission that respects the constraints scores better than a finished one that ignores them.
What to build
An order list holding 5,000 rows, generated in the browser. Each row: order number, customer, status (NEW |
PICKING | SHIPPED | CANCELLED), total, and a date.
It must have:
1. A search box filtering by order number.
2. A status filter accepting several statuses at once.
3. Row click opens a side panel showing that order’s detail.
4. Keyboard operation: arrow keys move the selected row, Enter opens the panel, Escape closes it and
returns focus to the row that was open.
Constraints
Constraint
1. The list must stay printable. With a filter applied, Ctrl-P must produce every filtered row, not only the ones
on screen.
2. Typing in the search box must not re-render rows whose content has not changed - and you must prove
it.
3. The filter state lives in the URL. Reloading the page and pressing the browser back button both behave
correctly.
4. No useEffect. If you are convinced one is genuinely unavoidable here, use it and justify it in NOTES.md.
5. No dependencies beyond the framework, except one library of your choice for the table or list. Name it
and say why in NOTES.md.
6. Under 300 lines of your own code, excluding generated scaffolding and the data generator.
What to include
1. The source, without node_modules. It must start with a plain install then dev.
2. The proof for constraint 2 - a React DevTools Profiler recording (.json export) or screenshots showing
render counts for the same keystroke before and after your optimisation, with the numbers stated. If your
first attempt already had no wasted renders, show the recording that demonstrates it and say so.
3. NOTES.md, 400 words maximum:
● How you satisfied constraints 1 and 2 together, and what you gave up to do it.
● Three decisions you made, each with the alternative you rejected and what would have to be
true for the rejected one to be correct.
● Anything you did not finish, stated plainly.
We run your submission and check every constraint against it, including reproducing the measurement in point 2.   Submission
Create a public GitHub repository named frontend-assessment-yourname, containing:
Path Contents
PART-A.md (or PART-A.pdf) Your answers to the thirteen questions, with the position you applied for at the top
/app The Part B project
/app/NOTES.md As specified above
/app/evidence/ The profiler recording or screenshots
README.md How to install and run it, in the fewest steps that work
Commit as you work. A repository whose entire history is one commit pushed at the deadline tells us nothing and
counts against you. i gavethe whole project contet above and we will work on part B prject so im gonna give you step-by-step Work Breakdown Structure (WBS) so you build the project accrding to my instuction beacuse there should not be one whole comit for the project then we will build it step by step and comit each progress here is the first task you should do Phase 1: Foundation (Setup & Data)
Start by establishing the project skeleton and the mock data.

Step 1: Initialize the Project

Action: Scaffold the Vite project, clear out all boilerplate CSS/components, and set up basic styling (e.g., standard CSS or Tailwind if you prefer, though plain CSS keeps line counts lower).
